statement: Cross-domain tenant-administrator provisioning and same-tenant user governance must remain distinct capabilities while all three backoffices expose user and role management.
scope: merchant and agent tenant administrator provisioning
email login identifiers and identity mapping
given: three isolated account domains and application sessions
application identity mapping keyed by issuer and subject
when: a platform administrator lists users across account domains
a platform administrator creates or maintains a merchant or agent system administrator
a protected platform administrator resets a precisely bound merchant or agent local/test password
a merchant or agent administrator manages an ordinary user or role
a new login identity is created
then: Only PLATFORM system administrators may read the cross-domain directory, and its account-domain filter defaults to PLATFORM.

PLATFORM cross-domain writes may affect only protected system-administrator Memberships in an existing MERCHANT or AGENT Tenant, except that a protected PLATFORM system administrator may reset an ACTIVE local/test password for a precisely bound MERCHANT or AGENT User without changing lifecycle status or roles.
Ordinary user and role administration derives tenant and account domain from the trusted Session and rejects client tenant selectors.
Tenant affiliation is stored as Membership and is not duplicated as merchantId, agentId, tenantId, portal, or realm fields on User.
A PLATFORM provisioning actor never receives or impersonates a target-tenant Membership, and cross-domain audit records do not forge a target-tenant operator.
New login identifiers are normalized email addresses, while identity mapping remains the exact issuer and subject pair and the same email may represent independent Users in different account domains.
counterexamples: a merchant or agent request selects another tenant with tenantId
a platform operator assigns arbitrary ordinary roles to a target tenant user through the cross-domain endpoint
merchantId or agentId is added to User as the authorization source
a platform actor is stored as though it held a Membership in the target tenant
email is used instead of issuer and subject to merge or map identities
a new non-email username is accepted
